I'm not able to reproduce this issue on Arch Linux, X11, on AMD 6750 XT. Could be specific to your setup, maybe graphics drivers, or having a multi-monitor setup (which I don't have).

Can you try testing earlier dev builds of Godot [between 4.4.1 and 4.5](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/#4.5), to narrow down which version introduced this issue?

I'm also unable to reproduce:

> Godot v4.5.stable - Linux Mint 22.1 (Xia) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti (nvidia; 570.133.07) - AMD Ryzen 9 3900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory

> Can you try testing earlier dev builds of Godot [between 4.4.1 and 4.5](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/#4.5), to narrow down which version introduced this issue?

Thank you for the swift support! I have just tried all versions between 4.4.1 and 4.5, and it seems that the issue is introduced in v4.5.beta6.official [d5ad0556a], with beta5 having no issues whatsoever. I am no means an academic on godot, so I am unsure what might be different betwen the versions to cause this issue, but until I updated from 4.4.1 to 4.5 I had no issues using the panel, on my current setup.

I can provide a video if needed, along with other information that you might need in order to help diagnose the issue. 

Cheers!

Could you also please provide the stack trace when Godot crashes? You'll need to open your project directly from the command line, not from the project manager:

Try running the following commands and check the output (both should return `false`), `AccessKit` code should not be called if you are not using screen reader (it seems to be quite buggy on Linux):

```
dbus-send --dest=org.a11y.Bus --print-reply /org/a11y/bus org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get string:org.a11y.Status string:IsEnabled
```

```
dbus-send --dest=org.a11y.Bus --print-reply /org/a11y/bus org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get string:org.a11y.Status string:ScreenReaderEnabled
```

> AccessKit related crash it looks like.
> 
> Disable accessibility/accesskit in Godot settings and it should go away

I am quite the noob and unsure of where and how to disable these settings, I will try to see if it is something I can manage on my end, seeing as not many others are having this issue. Also, thank you for the support, you guys catch on to these things crazy fast!!!

> I am quite the noob and unsure of where and how to disable these settings `Editor` (menu) → `Editor Settings`, in the dialog `Interface` → `Accessibility` → `Accessibility Support`, set it to "Disabled".

FIXED!

Thank you!!!

> `Editor` (menu) → `Editor Settings`, in the dialog `Interface` → `Accessibility` → `Accessibility Support`, set it to "Disabled".

You guys are all legends, something so simple but sometimes a pain to figure out for the average user, you guys take your time out of the day to help, I can't be more grateful!

I certainly hope anyone who gets the same issue is able to find this thread going forward :D

I'm not sure if I'm the one who should be closing this thread so I will leave it as is but know that I don't have anymore problems, you guys are doing great work out here!
No, please leave it as there is clearly some sort of an issue with dbus/AccessKit itself

Hi there,

Not sure exactly what is leading to these crashes but I'm making them impossible in https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit/pull/621.

The fact that AccessKit gets initialized for so many users who apparently don't have any assistive technology running on their system is concerning and I am not sure what is the best course of actions there. We are playing by the rules so I'm starting to wonder if some Linux distributions force accessibility to always be enabled.

> Not sure exactly what is leading to these crashes but I'm making them impossible in

It almost certainly has something to do with the creation and destruction of windows, but I was not able to determine the exact cause. The issue is extremely inconsistent.

> We are playing by the rules so I'm starting to wonder if some Linux distributions force accessibility to always be enabled.

All distros I have tested seems to behave correctly, but we got a bunch of issues from the same distros  (this is the first one when both dbus properties are set), so it might be caused by a specific app (something is abusing accessibility API to circumvent screen/input capture restrictions?), and not a distro issue.

I have found another issue hitting this exact same bug with a bunch of people running different distributions and presumably no assistive technology: https://github.com/JHDev2006/Super-Mario-Bros.-Remastered-Public/issues/89
@bruvzg I've just released [accesskit-c 0.17.1](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/releases/tag/0.17.1) which contain the fix for this bug.

> I've just released [accesskit-c 0.17.1](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/releases/tag/0.17.1) which contain the fix for this bug.

I'll test in and update our custom build repo on Saturday.

At least it is less random, and might be easier to debug, so I'll try to reproduce it with a simple project instead of editor a bit later.
Unfortunately this stack trace doesn't point to the exact place where the crash occur. If you can give me reliable steps to reproduce, I might be able to see what happens on our side.

> If you can give me reliable steps to reproduce, I might be able to see what happens on our side. - Open any project in the editor (creating new empty project will work). - Select 3D tab. - Open sun preview popup (`⋮` button). - Select and enter edit text for any of the values (it is not crashing if it's editor with slider). - Close the popup (click outside it). - It is crashing when popup is closed.

@bruvzg I still don't have the proper setup to hunt this bug, but I have prepared a [modified version of the bindings](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/tree/tree-capture). You'd have to set the `ACCESSKIT_CAPTURE_PATH` environment variable to a JSONL file that I'd appreciate you sending to me if you happen to trigger the bug. Hopefully this file will allow me to replay the sequence of events that led to the crash.

Also, we've just released [accesskit-c 0.18](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/releases/tag/0.18.0) which contain changes in how we initialize on *nix platforms: detecting if an AT is running, not if accessibility is enabled on the system. This should finally prevent users who don't need AccessKit to hit this bug in the first place.
I'll check this Friday.

Bug fixed in https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit/pull/661, should be included in the next release of our C bindings. Please note however that it seemed to hide a bug in Godot as the tree update right after the panic causes another panic.
[accesskit-c 0.19](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/releases/tag/0.19.0) is released. It contains the aforementioned bug fix.
